title: Solve two-step equations (3x + 4 = 16) by undoing operations in order

lesson.title: Undo in the Right Order: 3x + 4 = 16

steps.say: You already know how to build an equation on a balance scale. Today we learn the one trick that actually solves it: undoing the operations in the right order. Think of it like taking off your shoes and socks. Socks went on first, shoes went on second, so shoes come off first.

visual.caption: Both sides weigh the same, so the scale is level

steps.say: Here is what happened to x. First it got multiplied by three, then four was added on. So to undo it, we go backwards: peel off the plus four first, and deal with the times three second. Always the adding or subtracting first, the multiplying or dividing second.

visual.caption: Peel off the +4 first, then handle the ×3

steps.say: Step one: take four away. But here is the golden rule of the balance — whatever you take off the left, you must take off the right, or the scale tips. Sixteen take away four is twelve, so now we have three x equals twelve.

visual.caption: Take 4 off both sides — still balanced

steps.say: Step two: three x means three equal bags of x, and together they weigh twelve. So share the twelve into three equal groups. Twelve divided by three is four, so x equals four. Check it: three times four is twelve, plus four is sixteen. It works.

visual.caption: 12 shared into 3 equal bags → each bag is 4

steps.say: Now the three traps I see all the time. Trap one: dividing before subtracting, turning three x plus four into x plus four equals sixteen over three. No — the plus four is still stuck on, so it has to go first. Trap two: seeing three x equals twelve and subtracting the three to get nine. But three x means three times x, not three plus x, so you divide, and you get four. Trap three: dividing only the left side and writing x equals twelve. That tips the scale. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.

visual.caption: Dividing only the left tips the scale — that is wrong

steps.say: So remember: undo the plus or minus first, then undo the times or divide, and always do it to both sides.

lesson.answer: Undo the adding first, the multiplying second — and always do it to both sides.

practice.question: You and your friends are buying movie tickets in Vancouver. You buy five tickets that all cost the same, plus a bag of popcorn that costs seven dollars. The total is fifty-two dollars. If t stands for the price of one ticket, the equation is five t plus seven equals fifty-two. What is t? (Try writing the two steps down yourself.)
practice.answer: t equals nine dollars. First take seven off both sides: fifty-two minus seven is forty-five, so five t equals forty-five. Then divide both sides by five: forty-five divided by five is nine. Check: five times nine is forty-five, plus seven is fifty-two.
